query:
Which member made the argument about structured effort over elevation, stating that the Ridge loop 'turns into a sufferfest', while another member later expressed dissatisfaction with the same shorter route alternative, calling it essentially not worth doing?

Options:
A. Tomás
B. Marcus
C. Derek
D. Lena
context:
[1] (about=Derek, episodic, t0 @2026-01-10T08:31:00) For what it is worth, I will vote Valley flat. The Ridge loop always turns into a sufferfest with that climb section, and people end up strung out for the last 20km. A proper structured start to the year is more sensible than chasing elevation numbers.
[2] (about=Marcus, episodic, t16 @2026-03-07T13:21:00) Right. Noted. And for reference the group seemed to think everyone enjoys those long flat circuits near Millfield. That is not quite right. I do not enjoy flat circuits. I never have. The Cranfield ridge section is exactly the kind of terrain I want more of.
[3] (about=Lena, episodic, t18 @2026-03-14T14:02:00) From a physio perspective the dual-route model also allows better load management at the individual level. Unanimous support for it seems right to me. Though I want to flag something. The consensus that 'everyone prefers dual-route' may be slightly false. Marcus, you originally pushed for a single hard route as the standard. Is this a genuine shift?
[4] (about=Ben, core, t0 @2026-01-10T08:15:00) Flexible on route; in either way, Ridge sounds fun if the climb is taken slow.
[5] (about=Callum, core, t0 @2026-01-10T08:15:00) Votes Ridge loop; 650m is nothing once moving, Valley flat has zero measurable power data worth tracking.
[6] (about=Callum, core, t2 @2026-01-17T11:47:00) Today's ride data: Cranfield Ridge loop, 82.4km, 648m elevation, avg power 187w; segment times in link.
[7] (about=Derek, core, t0 @2026-01-10T08:15:00) Votes Valley flat; Ridge loop becomes a sufferfest with strung-out riders, prefers a structured start to the year.
[8] (about=Lena, episodic, t15 @2026-03-07T13:10:00) I need to say something about today. The Cranfield ridge section, the 10% gradient past the farm, I have been avoiding anything above 8% for over a year because of my hip flexor. I rode it today. All of it. And it was fine.
[9] (about=GROUP, said_by=Marcus, group-interaction, t0 @2026-01-10T08:15:00) First ride of the year: Ridge loop (Cranfield Ridge, 82km, 650m) chosen over Valley flat. Vote by 9pm Friday, regroup at every summit, 8am Saturday start at usual layby.
[10] (about=Priya, core, t0 @2026-01-10T08:15:00) Prefers Ridge loop over Valley flat; considers Valley flat a warm-up, not a first-ride-of-the-year vibe.
[11] (about=Saoirse, core, t0 @2026-01-10T08:15:00) Votes Ridge loop; the descent past Cranfield Farm is why she joined the group.
[12] (about=Saoirse, core, t2 @2026-01-17T11:47:00) Cranfield Ridge loop has a bit of gravel at the third hairpin but nothing serious; suggests doing it again in summer when dry.
[13] (about=GROUP, said_by=Tomás, group-interaction, t16 @2026-03-07T13:12:00) Next Saturday's ride will have two options: one with the Cranfield ridge section for climbers, option B flatter for anyone who wants it. Route vote Thursday.
agent_answer:
Derek made the argument about structured effort over elevation, calling the Ridge loop a “sufferfest.”  
Marcus later expressed dissatisfaction with the flatter alternative, saying he does not enjoy flat circuits and prefers the Ridge terrain.

So: **Derek (C)** made the argument; **Marcus (B)** later disagreed with the shorter/flatter route.
